definition: In computer vision, object co-segmentation is a special case of image segmentation, which is defined as jointly segmenting semantically similar objects in multiple images or video frames.
details: In computer vision, object co-segmentation is a special case of image segmentation, which is defined as jointly segmenting semantically similar objects in multiple images or video frames.

explainer.lead: Object co-segmentation jointly segments semantically similar objects across multiple images or video frames. It matters because it exploits shared appearance instead of treating each image alone.

tiers.eli5: Show it several photos each containing a bicycle, and it learns to cut out the bicycle in all of them together, rather than one at a time.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to get masks without per-image labels, and a common pitfall is that a group of images lacking a genuinely shared object yields unstable masks.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a set of images, produce per-image pixel masks for the objects judged semantically similar across the set; it is a special case of image segmentation and relies on cross-image similarity, so performance depends on how consistent the shared object appears.

explainer.example: Given several photos of the same dog in different rooms, the method outputs a mask around the dog in every photo.
